title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
snippet: Information about a cognizable offence must be recorded by the officer in charge; oral information is reduced to writing, read over, and signed; a copy is given free to the informant.

title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
snippet: Information may be given electronically; the officer may take action on it and the person may be required to sign within three days, supporting remote and urgent reporting.

title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
snippet: Police officers have powers to investigate cognizable cases; where investigation is refused or stalled, hierarchical remedies including approach to Superintendent of Police and Magistrate may apply as per the Act.

title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
snippet: Any police station can register information about a cognizable offence irrespective of territorial jurisdiction and transfer it to the competent station, enabling zero FIR for urgent cases.

title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
snippet: Judicial Magistrates may take cognizance and order investigation in accordance with the Sanhita when legally moved; useful when police do not register or investigate.

title: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
snippet: Evidence rules recognise electronic and digital records; preserving screenshots, call logs, and hashes helps investigation and trial.

title: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
snippet: FIR in atrocity cases should be registered promptly; wrongful neglect by public servants is punishable; anticipatory bail is barred for several offences under the Act.

title: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
snippet: Offences against children must be reported; police and Special Juvenile Police Unit handle investigation with child-friendly procedures and confidentiality.

title: Indian Penal Code, 1860
snippet: Many serious offences are cognizable where police can arrest without warrant and must register FIR on information; schedule in BNSS and IPC determines powers.

title: National Human Rights Commission guidelines
snippet: Complaints of death or torture in custody can be lodged with NHRC and State Human Rights Commissions in addition to FIR and Magistrate inquest where applicable.

title: Anonymized FIR registration · Pune district
section: Illustrative outcome: FIR registered after SP office letter
snippet: Anonymized legal-literacy notes from Pune district: after a station diary entry but no FIR for a cognizable theft, the complainant submitted a written complaint to the Superintendent of Police with itemised bills and CCTV stills; an FIR was registered and investigation assigned. Paths differ by facts; not a reported judgment.

title: Anonymized FIR attempt · Pune district
section: Illustrative outcome: preliminary inquiry, delayed registration
